sentences.text: The instant petition has been preferred by the petitioners under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking direction from this Court to command the Respondents 1 to 4 to release the pending awarded amount to the tune of Rs. 54,97,500/- in favour of Petitioner No. 1, Rs. 7,27,500/- in favour of Petitioners 2 to 4 and Rs. 24,66,500/- in favour of Petitioner No. 5, respectively along with interest without any further delay.

2. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the Petitioner No. 1 was the owner in possession of land measuring 05 Kanals 13 Marlas, falling under Khasra No. 431, situated at Village Haspalote, Tehsil Thannamandi District Rajouri; Petitioners 2 to 4 were the owners of land measuring 15 Marlas, falling under Khasra No. 421, situated at Village Haspalote, Tehsil Thannamandi District Rajouri; and Petitioner No. 5 was the owner of land measuring 02 Kanals 11 Marlas, falling under Khasra No. 593, situated at Village Haspalote, Tehsil Thannamandi District Rajouri.

He further submits that the respondents had initiated the acquisition proceedings in respect of the aforesaid land and accordingly Notification under Section 4 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act 1990, Svt was issued by Respondent No. 5 vide notice dated 02.03.2018 and pursuant thereto, the objections were called within 15 days from the date of issuance of said notification, however, no objections were received during the prescribed period and the case was submitted to the District Collector (Deputy Commissioner) Rajouri vide communication dated 14.07.2018 for issuance of declaration under Section 6 and 7 of the Land Acquisition Act, which were then issued by the Commissioner/Secretary to Government, Revenue Department vide endorsement No. 25.09.2018.

Pursuant thereto, notice under Section 9 & 9 A of the Land Acquisition Act was issued by Respondent No. 4 vide communication dated 03.10.2018 to the interested persons and the indenting department for filing of objections, if any.

However, no objections were received and the land owners have shown their willingness and after fulfilling all the requisite formalities, the matter was returned to the office of Respondent No. 4 by Tehsildar Thannamandi vide communicated dated 15.10.2018.

The further case of the petitioners is that the rate of compensation of the land in question was fixed by Tehsildar Thanndamandi @ Rs. 10Lacs Per Kanal alongwith Jabrana @ 15% and Administrative charges @ 1% and thus, an amount to the tune of Rs. 1,19,63,450/- was fixed to be paid to the petitioners for acquisition of their landed property for the construction of road for public purposes.

That on the basis of above mentioned assessment made by revenue authorities, Respondent No. 5 had passed final award of Rs.
1,19,63,450/- in favour of the petitioners vide award dated 18.10.2019.

That in terms of award supra,
Respondent No. 5 prepared apportionment statement of land of the petitioners which came under the alignment of the road and thus acquired by the respondents, details of which are reflected as under:

sentences.text: The further case of the petitioners is that, due to the delay on the part of Respondents 1 to 4 in releasing the payment, the petitioners had approached them and requested them to release the amount which is lying pending with them with regard to the land in question, due to which Respondent No. 3 submitted a communication dated 16.11.2019 before Respondent No. 2, whereby a request was made to him to arrange funds with respect to land compensation.

Despite the issuance of the abovementioned communication, nothing was done on behalf of the respondents with regard to the release of pending amount and accordingly, the petitioners have preferred the instant petition.

5. Detailed objections have been filed by Mr. Ravinder Gupta, learned AAG on behalf of Respondents 1 to 4, wherein at Para 11 of their reply, they have admitted that an amount of Rs. 19.00Lacs has been released in favour of Respondent No. 5 i.e. SDM Thannamandi for further disbursement in favour of the legal owners.

It has been further submitted that an amount of Rs. 99.45Lacs has been demanded from Higher Authority vide communication dated 24.02.2022 but till date no payment has been released from the Higher Authority and has further pleaded that as and when the funds are made available, payment will be released in favour of the lawful claimants including the petitioners.

6. In light of the stand taken by Respondents 1 to 4 in their objections both the parties submit that the instant petition can be disposed of at this stage, by granting some reasonable time to the said respondents, so that the pending payment be released in favour of the lawful claimants including the petitioners, to which the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents have no objection.

7. In view of the above and with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties,
the instant petition is disposed of along with connected application(s), if any, by directing Respondents 1 to 4 to deposit the compensation amount which is payable to the lawful claimants including the petitioners before Respondent No. 5 i.e. SDM Thannamandi within a period of six weeks from the date, copy of this order is supplied to the office of Respondents 1 to 4 by the petitioners and subject to compensation amount being deposited before Respondent No. 5 by Respondents 1 to 4 within the aforesaid period, the disbursement of compensation shall be made to the lawful claimants including the petitioners within two weeks thereafter, after proper verification.

The writ petition stands disposed of in the manner indicated above.
